data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, ), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.name: Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars (CRISM)
record.description: The Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars (CRISM) on the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter is a hyperspectral imaging spectrometer designed to map the surface mineralogy of Mars. In particular it will be looking for evidence of aqueous and hydrothermal deposits and other mineralogical indicators of water. It will be used to search for layering of surface features and will monitor the pattern and density of dust and ice clouds. CRISM will measure 560 individual wavelengths of sunlight reflected from the surface in the range from 400 to 4050 nanometers (visible to shortwave infrared) at 6.55 nanometers/channel. At a nominal 300 km altitude CRISM has a field of view 18 meters wide and 10.8 km long, with a spatial resolution of 18 meters. Over the first year of the mission CRISM will map the entire planet at a resolution of 100 to 200 meters. Based on these maps, targets will be selected for higher resolution imaging. Total estimated cost of CRISM is $17.6 million.
